newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Treasury tenders 2007 bond as rally rolls on.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Treasury tenders 2007 bond as rally rolls on.

text.p: The Swiss Treasury sold a total of 150 million Swiss francs of its outstanding 4-1/2 percent June 2007 bond to banks Wednesday in a move which dealers noted came in the midst of what has become a protracted bond rally.

The Treasury said Wednesday morning that it had tendered 150 million francs of a portion of the Confederate 2007 which it had held as reserve. The "007" bond was already reopened in an auction in January which was completed on January 23.
The January reopening of the bond led to allocation of 904 million francs to market participants, and brought the total outstanding to around 2.4 billion francs.
The Treasury reserved 300 million of the bond, and a portion of the reserve was what was tendered today.
A Treasury spokesman confirmed that the latest tranche of the issue was priced at 108.65, to yield 3.485 percent.
The issue has gained sharply from the January 23 auction, when it drew a price of 105.45, yielding 3.849 percent.
The spokesman said that the Treasury's action was aimed primarily at taking advantage of a good market.
"It seemed to us to be a convenient opportunity, because the markets have been going up in a near-constant fashion," the Treasury spokesman said.
One Swiss bond trader said the price on the latest offering seemed somewhat expensive to him after the latest price surge, but noted that there was still strong demand for the issue.
Dealers said offers for the latest tranche totaled 770 million Swiss francs.
Swiss bonds have staged a virtual nonstop rally since the start of the year. The average yield of federal bonds, at 3.39 percent on Wednesday, is at lows unseen since 1979.
The yield currently reflects bonds with a residual maturity of roughly 9.8 years.
